rule: A sandbox/containment boundary must be built from an object the contained party cannot reach (not a file in its cwd, an env var in its environment, or a permission bit on a tree it owns), and layered defenses must be attack-tested together rather than validated in isolation.

Optimize session length and tool-output verbosity (not instruction-file size) for cost: compact at phase boundaries, pipe Bash/Read output through head, offload noisy investigation to subagents, since every context token is re-read on every subsequent turn.

Before treating agreement across multiple independent review lanes as confirmation of a claim, check what each lane actually cited; if they all trace to the same secondary artifact/memory sentence, that is N=1 evidence, not corroboration, and at least one lane must re-derive the claim from primary measurement data.

Treat a hook/guard/tool's own refusal or denial message as an unverified claim rather than a spec, and read the enforcing code (or probe with a harmless equivalent) before reporting to the founder that an action is blocked.

For findings that would trigger an expensive or alarming action (fabrication claims, security escalations, merge/publish gates), duplicate the verification check across independent vendors/reviewers rather than dividing the work between them, since division hides whether any single lane reached for the load-bearing evidence.

Before scaling a workload to 0 on the premise that data will be preserved, verify the volume backing is actually a PVC (not emptyDir) by inspecting the deployment's volume spec and confirming a matching PVC exists in the namespace.
check: A PreToolUse-hook (or wrapper-script) intercepting kubectl scale --replicas=0 commands that auto-runs `kubectl get pvc -n <ns>` and `.spec.template.spec.volumes` inspection, warning/blocking when no PVC backs the workload.
misses: Scale-downs performed via non-kubectl-scale paths (kubectl edit, kubectl apply with reduced replicas, Helm upgrade, ArgoCD sync/GitOps commit) that never pass through the wrapped command.

rule: Every Agent/Task/Workflow spawn from a coordinator session must set the `model` parameter explicitly; omitting it silently inherits the parent's (potentially most-expensive) tier for long-lived subagents.
check: A lint-rule/PreToolUse-hook that inspects Agent/Task/agent() tool-call arguments and flags or blocks any spawn where the `model` field is absent or null.

rule: Pipeline gates should warn-and-continue on recoverable structural issues and hard-block only on fatal ones; most stage failures are stochastic and should be re-run once before code changes are attempted; and every plan must carry an itemized validation checklist naming exact commands/outputs/thresholds rather than a bare 'verify it works' step.

When deciding whether a branch is safe to delete, judge its real change via merge-base/three-dot diff and actual issue/PR merged status, not a raw two-dot diff line count against current main, since a stale-cached worktree base produces phantom-deletion diffs.
check: A wrapper-script for branch-cleanup tooling that always computes `git diff <merge-base> branch` (or three-dot `origin/main...branch`) and queries the GitHub API for PR/issue merged status before allowing deletion, rather than accepting a raw two-dot diff.
misses: Manual/ad-hoc `git branch -d`/`git push --delete` invocations run outside the wrapper, and any restatement of the same stale-cache root cause in a different tool that isn't routed through this script.

rule: Before trusting any claim that an LLM-as-judge/scorer is 'locked' or deterministic, run a dedicated self-consistency test — rescore a frozen, byte-identical set of already-generated outputs repeatedly under the same judge config and measure the flip rate — separately from generator-side reproducibility checks.
check: A CI-job that rescoring a frozen fixture set N times with the judge held at fixed config, computing label-flip rate via deterministic comparison, and failing the build if flip rate exceeds a set threshold.
misses: A 'locked scorer' claim asserted in a written report or memory entry outside the pipeline that never invokes the CI job at all, or a fixture set that doesn't actually match the production judge/config combination.

rule: When landing multiple same-repo PRs, land them serially and re-run the CI gate after each merge (since each PR's CI is only valid against the main that existed when it last ran), and treat a failing gate as a hard stop rather than merging anyway.
check: Branch-protection required-status-checks (or a modified `cli-dispatch land` that reads the gate result for the PR's current merge-ref and refuses to invoke the merge API when it reports failing).
misses: Cross-PR semantic conflicts that only appear after a second PR merges — the mechanism only catches red-on-request-to-merge, it does not itself enforce that the serial land+re-gate sequence happens rather than two lands firing close together without an intervening re-gate.

rule: 'Merged to main' does not mean 'live in the current working environment' — verify a change against the actual on-disk load path of the current working tree/branch/session, and check whether the artifact has more than one install source (repo-tracked path plus a separate make-install/build/copy step) that could silently reintroduce the old state.

Never wrap a run_in_background Bash call's command in `nohup ... &` (or trail it with sleep/tail) — pass the real long-running command directly as the tool call's foreground command so the harness tracks the actual process instead of a wrapper that exits early and fires a meaningless completion notification.
check: A PreToolUse-hook on the Bash tool that, when run_in_background=true, pattern-matches the command string for `nohup` or a trailing backgrounding `&` and blocks/warns before execution.
